Most of Earth's oxygen today comes from the ocean, not from land plants or trees [d4][d8]. According to the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, "more than half the planet's oxygen comes from the ocean," specifically from the top 200 meters, produced by photosynthetic organisms [d4]. The Smithsonian Ocean portal confirms that "more than half of the oxygen you breathe comes from marine photosynthesizers, like phytoplankton and seaweed," with the cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus alone responsible for producing 20% of atmospheric oxygen [d8]. The Planetary Society similarly states that "photosynthetic organisms in Earth's oceans produce roughly half of the planet's oxygen" today [d5]. Some sources estimate the ocean's contribution even higher—around 70–72%—with phytoplankton alone accounting for approximately 50%, while trees and rainforests contribute only about 28% [d1][d2][d6].
